narrative.overview:
This file records the interface as it shipped at the end of plan task 17 (commit ab9d705). Every value here is read from `src/ui/tokens.css` and the four style sheets beside it. `test/unit/design-record.test.ts` checks the record against the code, and `test/unit/contrast.test.ts` checks the palette.

The product is a factory you lay out: lanes, the routes between them, and tasks moving through. The interface draws that floor the way a transit authority draws a network. A lane is a station. A transition is a line. Each outcome has its own line colour. A task is a small numbered train. A gate is a short bar on the line after its station. The same notation shrinks into a strip map wherever a run is listed.

The map is white in daylight ("map white") and deep blue at night ("night map"). The theme follows the system setting, and the button at the foot of the rail switches between Auto, Light and Dark. The world lends type, palette, density and the diagram. Navigation, layout and controls are the standard ones for a web tool.
keyCharacteristics: One meaning per colour, and a shape for every state.
Flat like print: panel tone and 1px lines, no shadow on the map.
Dense: 28px controls and rows, 8px inside a group, 16px between groups.
State steps. Nothing fades or slides.
The page keeps to the window. Each part scrolls by itself.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Through blue means passed. Return vermilion means failed. Signal yellow with an ink border means a person can act. End grey means nothing is happening. Ink is text, selection and focus. None of them is decoration, a link colour or a highlight. Links are ink, underlined. A diff uses neither blue nor vermilion.

rules.name: The Palette Only Rule
rules.body: No colour is written outside `tokens.css`. The style sheets use `var(--name)` and `color-mix` of those. One exception: the tab's icon in `src/ui/tab.ts` writes the rail's navy and the signal yellow as plain colours, because an icon cannot read the palette.

rules.name: The Yellow Is Yours Rule
rules.body: Signal yellow appears only on what a person can act on: the Approve and Answer buttons and the "Decide in the inbox" link, the rail's count, the mark of a row or lane that waits, the stop that asked on a strip map, a train that waits, the route that asks a person (on the map, in the legend and in the inspector), the inbox end station, and the station of a run that asked.

rules.name: The Rule And Edge Rule
rules.body: `--rule` is the hairline between things. `--edge` is the border of a control and must be seen: at least 3:1.

rules.name: The Contrast Rule
rules.body: `test/unit/contrast.test.ts` computes the contrast of the palette in both themes: 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for shapes and lines. Two things are deliberately not held to it. The text of a disabled control is end grey. The lines, tags and ends of the workflow step back to opacity 0.28 while a run is drawn over the map, so the run reads first.

rules.name: The Fixed Scale Rule
rules.body: Text sizes are in rem and nothing scales with the viewport.

rules.name: The State Steps Rule
rules.body: Nothing fades or slides. The style sheets hold no transition and no animation. A train is drawn at its lane and Replay moves it one step at a time.

rules.name: The Never Colour Alone Rule
rules.body: A state is told by its shape and its colour, and a line by its colour, its label and its end. The table above is the whole vocabulary.

dos: **Do** take every colour from `tokens.css`, and mix a hover or pressed tone from those with `color-mix`.
**Do** give every state a shape as well as a colour, from the table under Shapes.
**Do** put an ink border (1.5px) or an ink casing on anything signal yellow.
**Do** border a control with `--edge` and divide things with `--rule`.
**Do** keep a new screen inside the window: its parts scroll, the page does not.
**Do** add a pair to `test/unit/contrast.test.ts` when text or a shape lands on a new ground.
donts: **Don't** use signal yellow on anything a person cannot act on.
**Don't** use through blue or return vermilion for anything but passed and failed. A diff, a link and a highlight are ink.
**Don't** add a transition or an animation.
**Don't** add a colour for one screen. Five meanings, five colours.
**Don't** use gradients, glows or glass as decoration, and don't put a shadow on the map. The one gradient in the build is the checker behind a screenshot.
**Don't** lay content out as a grid of cards.
**Don't** decorate with map furniture that carries no information: no roundel logos, compass roses or fare zones.
**Don't** use any game's name, art or icons.
